author: Harshil Mathur
body:
The digital-native generation is more willing to spend on unique experiences, but they are far less forgiving of friction in shopping.

A decade ago, amid the price-sensitive instincts of millennials and Gen X, a phenomenon such as the experience economy could not have thrived. A young person today is likely to purchase premium tickets to a Diljit Dosanjh or Coldplay concert, pay with instant credit, have gig essentials like power banks and glitter delivered to their doorstep, and reserve a pre-gig meal near the venue.

The digitally-native Gen Z’s willingness to adopt unique, frictionless services is quietly shaping a new model of commerce. Businesses must understand this 377 million-strong cohort if they want to centre innovation on its specific needs.

Speed, trust, and the death of patience

Born with the internet, Gen Z has little experience of a world without instant gratification. They are digital-first in the truest sense: cash-on-delivery (CoD) is fading, and checkout patience is near zero. The shift is reflected in Razorpay’s data, which shows that over 80% of Gen Z digital transactors prefer UPI or other online payments, signalling that CoD is less central to their behaviour compared with other online cohorts (including Millennials and above) while transacting in the same e-commerce category.

Gen Z sees the internet as an integrated environment, not just a tool. Where millennials may forgive a failed transaction and quietly retry, Gen Z speaks up immediately when something breaks. This difference is reflected in engagement data: over the last six months, Gen Z merchants submitted significantly more support tickets, while millennials raised far fewer. For Gen Z, seamless experiences are the baseline, and there is no room for startups to pitch buggy offerings.

Gen Z is more open to spending where they feel a sense of connection and trust, whether it is the 10-minute delivery of a curated outfit for a last-minute party or the frenzy surrounding a limited-edition ‘drop’ from a creator-led clothing label. We expect this to bring about explosive growth in D2C commerce.

In the B2B realm, too, the Gen Z entrepreneur or manager views business transactions through the same lens. They have little to no patience for long sales calls. They want self-service, transparent pricing and instant onboarding. A B2B product tethered to a weeks-long demo-to-delivery cycle is effectively invisible to this generation.

Tailored and swift finance

Gen Z’s relationship with money is different, too. They would rather not go to a bank for a loan, preferring to obtain credit at the point of purchase instead. This is boosting “contextual credit”, or embedded finance, where credit cards linked to food delivery or ecommerce platforms see far higher adoption than traditional plastic cards.

Another example is UPI. Millennials are less likely to trust merchants with saved payment methods, whereas Gen Z is more comfortable using UPI’s recurring payment feature. Among Gen Z merchants, adoption of AutoPay has outpaced all other demographics, posting a meteoric 42-fold year-on-year rise.

The same logic extends to insurance. Digital natives prefer it bundled with products, whether it be travel insurance with flight bookings, device insurance with electronics purchases, or coverage for a high-stakes concert ticket, integrated directly into the checkout flow. They are practical and informed, and they expect financial services to anticipate their needs rather than interrupt their journey.

Building for the $2-trillion opportunity

To capture a slice of the projected $2 trillion in influenced spending, startups and businesses must focus on building for hyper-speed without compromising on security. It also means moving away from banking by appointment to finance on demand. Gen Z-led businesses are opting out of traditional relationship banking entirely, preferring automated, self-service tools that move at the speed of their code.

In this new economic reality, founders are increasingly asking whether their infrastructure is truly Gen Z–ready. While trust for earlier generations was often built on legacy and longevity, Gen Z evaluates trust continuously --shaped by every seamless, frictionless and instinctively “vibe-checked” interaction. This shift signals a new form of commerce, one that brands must actively re-examine and design for --building experiences that feel native to how this generation discovers, decides and transacts.

(The author is the CEO and cofounder of the fintech platform Razorpay)
